founders-and-forks.title: Founders, investors and the fork
founders-and-forks.note: One argument in three parts: who investors choose and why, a deal a founder with leverage could offer instead, and what keeps every side honest once control is out of the contract.

items.label: 1 · The choice
items.title: The controllable founder
items.line: Why investors may pick the founder they can steer, and what record labels taught us about who the commodity is.

items.label: 2 · The deal
items.title: Sell, don't issue
items.line: The investor buys the founder's shares, the founder lends the company what it needs, and nobody buys the steering wheel.

items.label: 3 · The protection
items.title: The fork next door
items.line: Founders, customers and investors are each protected from the others because anyone can fork, and forks win only after a breakdown.

sgit-ruflo.title: SGit × Ruflo: one run, five ways in

decision-policy.title: Agent decision policies: a series in four parts
decision-policy.note: How did the agent decide? Behaviour, decision and workflow as three policies; approving at altitude so it scales; case law for the cases nobody predicted; and three scenarios mapped.

items.title: Three policies for an agent
items.line: Behaviour says what it may do, decision says who chooses, workflow says in what order; zoom into one cell and it becomes both.

items.label: 2 · Altitude
items.title: Approve at altitude
items.line: Decisions at every level, each allowed to narrow the one above and never to widen it, checked against declared envelopes.

items.label: 3 · Case law

items.line: Principles from the top, precedent from the cases, and how a decision earns its way into code.

items.label: 4 · Mapped

items.line: An agent's memory, this newsroom's release and a refund, element by element: defined, implemented, enforced, observed, verified.

less-code.title: Less code: a series in four parts
less-code.note: Code is a liability: remove what each use case does not call, apply it to the browser, and build on small blocks you did not have to write.

items.label: 1 · Measured
items.title: The minimum code below
items.line: One real use case of sgit, under coverage: 428 of 1,500 files ran, and a tree of only those passed.

items.label: 2 · Less code
items.title: The code you do not ship
items.line: The worst bugs sit in features nobody needed; models make removing them safe, and someone can be paid to keep it small.

items.label: 3 · The browser
items.title: A minimal viable browser
items.line: A small kernel and components loaded when needed: a browser for one app, one agent, or a reader, sold as speed.

items.label: 4 · Small blocks
items.title: Cloudflare as Lego blocks
items.line: Storage, compute, models, email and identity as blocks, and an sgit vault server in 83 lines.
